questions.question: When 1 litre of water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C, its volume _____.
questions.questionHtml: When 1 litre of water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C, its volume _____.
questions.solution: In normal cases, the volume of substances increases on heating and decreases while cooling. When 1 litre of water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C, its volume increases due to 'Anomalous Expansion of Water'. The density of water is maximum at 4°C. When water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C, its density decreases. As density decreases, the volume increases. Volume = mass/density.

questions.question: To whom a Judge of the High Court will tender his resignation?
questions.questionHtml: To whom a Judge of the High Court will tender his resignation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the President of India.
Key Points
  • A High Court Judge is appointed by the President of India.
  • He is solely responsible for the appointment of any judge in a High Court. However, he may consult the Governor of the State, the acting Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Justice of that particular state’s High Court.
  • A High Court judge is also liable to get transferred to other High Courts.
  • This decision is entirely dependent on the Chief Justice of India.
  • The tenure of a High Court judge is not fixed by the Constitution but they hold office until they attain the age of 62 years.
  • A judge of the High Court can resign his office by writing to the President any time after the appointment.
Thus, a Judge of the High Court will tender his resignation to the President of India.

questions.question: The type of unemployment seen in India's agriculture sector is
questions.questionHtml: The type of unemployment seen in India's agriculture sector is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Disguised unemploymentKey Points

  • Disguised unemployment is found in the agricultural sector of India. Disguised unemployment is also known as hidden unemployment. In this type of unemployment, some people seem employed but they are actually not.
  • Disguised unemployment is when more people are involved in production then actually required.
  • On account of small land holdings , joint family systems, lack of alternative job opportunities there is disguised unemployment.

Additional Information

  • Frictional unemployment is a form of unemployment reflecting the gap between someone voluntarily leaving a job and finding another.
  • Open Unemployment refers to that economic phenomenon in which persons are able and willing to work at the prevailing wage rate but fail to get work. So, Open Unemployment is different from Disguised Unemployment. In the case of open unemployment, workers are totally idle
  • Cyclical unemployment is the component of overall unemployment that results directly from cycles of economic upturn and downturn. Unemployment typically rises during recessions and declines during economic expansions.

Thus, The type of unemployment seen in India's agriculture sector is Disguised unemployment.

questions.question: Which of the following states sometimes faces floods during the withdrawal of the monsoon phase?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following states sometimes faces floods during the withdrawal of the monsoon phase?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu

Important Points 

  • Tamil Nadu sometimes faces floods during the withdrawal of the monsoon phase.

Key Points

  • About Monsoon Withdrawal:
    • The withdrawal of the monsoon refers to the retreat of the monsoon winds from the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent,
    • usually beginning in early September and completing by the end of October.
    • During this phase, the reversal of winds occurs, leading to changes in rainfall patterns across the region.
    • In Tamil Nadu, the northeast monsoon brings significant rainfall during October to December
    • It can sometimes lead to flooding, especially when the withdrawal of the southwest monsoon coincides with heavy northeast monsoon rains.

questions.question: Which of the following Vakataka kings warned the grantees that their grants could be revoked if a conspiracy was hatched against the ruler?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Vakataka kings warned the grantees that their grants could be revoked if a conspiracy was hatched against the ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pravarsen II.

Key Points 

  • In the region of ancient Vidarbha, the core of which was Nagpur in north-east Maharashtra, a new power had emerged by the middle of the 3rd century CE.
  • This power was that of the Vakatakas, a new line of rulers started by Vindhyasakti.
  • Vakataka power soon became formidable and a branch was also established at Vatsagulma (modem Basim in Akola district).
  • The Vakataka family, later on, came into close contact with the Guptas, particularly after a matrimonial alliance was formed between the two families.
  • The most famous Vakataka king was Pravarasena-I of the main line, who alone had the title of Samrat among the Vakatakas.
  • He performed several Vedic sacrifices and issued many land grants to the Brahmanas.
  • The Vakatakas are known for a large number of copper plate land grants issued by them.
  • Pravarsen ll warned the grantees that their grants could be revoked if a conspiracy was hatched against the ruler.

Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which five year plan in India was based on the Harrod-Domar model?
questions.questionHtml: Which five year plan in India was based on the Harrod-Domar model?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is First Five Year Plan.

Key Points

  • Harrod-Domar model:-
    • It is an economic theory that explains the relationship between economic growth and investment.
    • The model emphasizes the importance of capital formation for economic development. 
  • First Five-Year Plan:-
    • It was launched in 1951, which focused on agriculture, irrigation, power, and transport.
    • It was based on the Harrod-Domar model.
    • The plan aimed to increase the country's national income and achieve self-sufficiency.

Additional Information

  • Third Five-Year Plan:-
    • It was implemented in 1961, which aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains, increase industrial production, and develop infrastructure. 
  • Fourth Five-Year Plan:-
    • It was launched in 1969, which aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.5% per annum, reduce poverty, and create employment opportunities.

questions.question: Where is the world’s highest motorable road, constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in October 2025, located?
questions.questionHtml: Where is the world’s highest motorable road, constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in October 2025, located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mig La Pass.

In News

  • The world’s highest motorable road, constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), is located at Mig La Pass in Ladakh, at an altitude of 19,400 feet above sea level.

Key Points

  • Project Himank surpassed its own Guinness World Record by constructing this road at Mig La Pass, overtaking the previous record set at Umling La (19,024 feet) in 2021.
  • The road, part of the Likaru-Mig La-Fukche alignment, has significant strategic importance and provides access to the Fukche village near the border.
  • The new road is expected to boost tourism in Ladakh, offering stunning views of the Indus Valley.
  • This achievement highlights the engineering excellence of BRO in building infrastructure in extreme and challenging terrains.

Additional Information

  • Border Roads Organisation (BRO)
    • The BRO is responsible for constructing and maintaining road networks in strategic areas, particularly in border regions.
    • BRO's work is critical for India’s defense preparedness and the development of remote areas in challenging terrains.
  • Project Himank
    • Project Himank is a major initiative of the BRO aimed at building roads in Ladakh’s high-altitude regions.
    • It has helped set world records in road construction and provides vital connectivity in the region.
  • Umling La and Mig La Pass
    • Umling La and Mig La Pass are both in Ladakh, known for being some of the world’s highest motorable roads.
  • Strategic Importance
    • The road through Mig La Pass is a vital axis for defense operations and enhancing connectivity in Ladakh.

questions.question: The President of India can be impeached for violation of the Constitution under which article?
questions.questionHtml: The President of India can be impeached for violation of the Constitution under which article?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Article 61.

Key Points

  • Procedure for impeachment of the President: 
    • When a President is impeached for violating the Constitution, either House of Parliament must support the charge. No such charge shall be preferred until it is accepted by not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House.
    • When either House of Parliament prefers an accusation, the other House investigates or causes the charge to be investigated, with the President having the right to appear and be served during the investigation.
    • If a resolution is passed as a result of the investigation, with not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House from which the charge was investigated or caused to be investigated, declaring that the charge preferred against the President has been sustained, such resolution would have the effect of excluding the President from office as of the date on which the resolution is passed.

Additional Information

  • On December 28, 1948, the Constituent Assembly debated Draft Article 50 (Article 61 of the Indian Constitution).
  • The process for removing the President of India from office was outlined in the Draft Article.

Important Points

Articles Explanation
Article 52 The President of India There shall be a President of India.
Article 74 Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
Article 78 Prime Minister's responsibilities in terms of providing information to the President, etc. It will be the Prime Minister's responsibility.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the organisation 'East India Association'?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following founded the organisation 'East India Association'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

Key Points

  • The East India Association was founded by Dadabhai Naoroji in 1866, in collaboration with Indians and retired British officials in London. 
  • It superseded the London Indian Society and was a platform for discussing matters and ideas about India, and to provide representation for Indians to the Government. 
  • The Association produced a journal (Journal of the East India Association) from its inception which included the papers that were delivered before their meetings.

Additional Information

  • Dadabhai Naoroji, the “Grand Old Man of India”, was the first Indian member of the British parliament.
  • In 1865 and 1866, Naoroji helped found the London Indian Society and the East India Association respectively.
  • He was Congress president thrice, in 1886, 1893, and 1906.
  • Dadabhai Naoroji was among the key proponents of the ‘Drain Theory’, disseminating it in his 1901 book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’.
  • Dadabhai Naoroji was born to a Gujarati-speaking Parsi family in Bombay, British India.
  • He formed the London India Society in 1865 to put forth views on Indian political, social and literary subjects. 
  • He was a founder-member of the Indian National Congress which he formed in 1885 along with Dinshaw Wacha and Allan Octavian Hume.
  • He also founded the Rahnumae Mazdayasne Sabha in 1851 to revive the Zoroastrian religion.
  • He died in 1917 in Bombay aged 91.

questions.question: How much reservation has the Haryana government announced for Agniveers in employment in April 2025?
questions.questionHtml: How much reservation has the Haryana government announced for Agniveers in employment in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 20%.

Key Points

  • The Haryana government has announced a 20% reservation for Agniveers in state government jobs starting from April 2025.
  • This decision is part of the state’s initiative to encourage youth participation in the Agnipath Scheme, launched by the central government.
  • The reservation applies to both Group C and Group D government jobs, ensuring that Agniveers have access to stable employment opportunities after their service in the armed forces.
  • The Agnipath Scheme allows youth to serve in the Indian Armed Forces for a short period (4 years). Haryana’s reservation policy is designed to ensure these individuals can transition smoothly to civilian life post-service.
  • This move by Haryana aligns with its policy to provide support and opportunities for ex-servicemen and those who have served in the armed forces. Hence, the correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

  • Agnipath Scheme:
    • The Agnipath Scheme was introduced by the Government of India in June 2022 to recruit youth for the armed forces for a tenure of 4 years.
    • The recruited personnel are called Agniveers. After completing their tenure, 25% of Agniveers are retained for a longer service in the armed forces, while the rest transition to civilian life.
    • The scheme aims to provide youth with a platform to serve their country while gaining valuable skills and training that can be utilized in future employment opportunities.
  • Haryana Government’s Reservation Policy:
    • The Haryana government’s decision to reserve 20% of jobs for Agniveers demonstrates its commitment to ensuring the welfare of individuals serving under the Agnipath Scheme.
    • This reservation policy is applicable in both Group C (clerical or semi-skilled positions) and Group D (unskilled workforce) categories of government employment.
    • This initiative encourages youth participation in national defense while addressing their post-service employment concerns.

Important Points

  • Benefits of the Reservation Policy:
    • The policy ensures that Agniveers, after completing their service tenure, have a secure career option in the public sector.
    • It highlights the state government’s recognition of the contribution of Agniveers to national security and their commitment to their welfare.
  • Other States’ Initiatives:
    • Several states like Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttarakhand have also announced reservation policies or employment opportunities for Agniveers.
    • These initiatives aim to provide Agniveers with a smooth transition to civilian life and ensure their skills are utilized effectively in various sectors.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Bhakti literature played a transformative role in Indian vernacular languages during the medieval period. Reason (R): The Bhakti saints composed works in local languages, making religious ideas accessible to the common people. Options:
questions.questionHtml:
Assertion (A): Bhakti literature played a transformative role in Indian vernacular languages during the medieval period.
Reason (R): The Bhakti saints composed works in local languages, making religious ideas accessible to the common people.

Options:

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.html: A is true, but R is false.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.html: A is false, but R is true.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.html: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.html: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 'C) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A'.

Key Points

  • Assertion (A): Bhakti literature played a transformative role in Indian vernacular languages during the medieval period.
    • This statement is correct.
    • Bhakti literature significantly influenced the development and popularity of vernacular languages across India, as it was one of the earliest large-scale literary movements to use local languages instead of Sanskrit or Persian.
    • This helped establish and enrich various regional languages, as Bhakti poetry and hymns were composed in languages like Tamil, Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, and Kannada.
  • Reason (R): The Bhakti saints composed works in local languages, making religious ideas accessible to the common people.
    • This statement is correct and provides the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
    • By using local languages, Bhakti saints such as Kabir, Tulsidas, Mirabai, and Tukaram made religious and philosophical ideas more accessible to ordinary people, transcending barriers of class, caste, and literacy.
    • This inclusivity allowed the Bhakti movement to reach a wider audience, fostering a sense of cultural unity and contributing to the development of Indian vernacular languages.

Explanation

  • Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) directly explains how Bhakti literature played a transformative role in Indian vernacular languages by making spiritual teachings accessible through local languages.

Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Additional Information

  • Impact of Bhakti Literature on Vernacular Languages:
    • Regional Identity: Bhakti literature helped create a distinct identity for various regional languages by standardizing and enriching them through devotional poetry and songs.
    • Prominent Bhakti Poets: Saints like Kabir (Hindi), Tulsidas (Awadhi), Tukaram (Marathi), and Basava (Kannada) made significant contributions to their respective languages.
    • Social Inclusion: By addressing universal themes of love, devotion, and equality, Bhakti literature transcended social hierarchies, appealing to people from all walks of life.

questions.question: Which force moves an aircraft through the air?
questions.questionHtml: Which force moves an aircraft through the air?
questions.solution: Thrust force moves an aircraft through the air. It overcomes drag and gravity, enabling forward motion. Drag force slows the aircraft, gravity pulls it downward, and lift force counteracts gravity to keep it airborne. Thrust is essential for propulsion and maintaining flight.
